implementation.instructions: Implement the scoped work described by the connected approved plan. Follow its accepted decisions and exclusions. Record the actual changes and unresolved gaps. This workflow intentionally has no separate validation stage: do not add a validation phase or claim validation passed. Report any checks actually performed and identify checks not run. Do not commit, push, or create the pull request; those are separate daemon-owned steps.

reasoning.instructions: Use the declared Tracer Bullets skill. Lead with a compact delivery map and new matters needing review. Order slices to prove, harden, then expand. Each slice names a demonstrable result, question proved, scope, dependencies, resolved inputs, execution detail, and observable validation. Keep detailed supporting material beneath its related change. Do not repeat the complete research or designs. Plan only: no implementation or delivery. Keep artifacts proportional to the task. Use generated evidence when available; otherwise identify the supplied source that covers a skipped stage. Never invent missing evidence or approval.

Prepare the PR document using the linked template and submit the text output with commitSubject, commitBody, prTitle, prBody, and changesetSnapshot. Copy changesetSnapshot exactly from the connected changeset.snapshotDigest. Ground the title and body in the supplied task, actual changes, and findings. This workflow skips a separate validation stage; say so clearly, distinguish checks actually performed from checks not run, and never imply an automated validation pass. Include unresolved blockers and relevant deferred work. Do not execute Git commands or publish the PR yourself.

Organize review around meaningful changes. Keep today versus proposed behavior, a concrete example or visual, rules, consequences, and the decision needed together. Summarize only current-state evidence needed for that change. If technical feedback changes the proposal, make that revision explicit. Keep artifacts proportional to the task. Use generated evidence when available; otherwise identify the supplied source that covers a skipped stage. Never invent missing evidence or approval.

Assess only the connected final reviewed document. Report whether it explicitly leaves a consequential unknown requiring investigation. Include concise evidence in reason. Ordinary caveats or already recorded future work do not imply a new unknown. Do not rewrite artifacts or approve work. Supply evidence only; the daemon evaluates it. Keep the response brief.

Group product and engineering questions by the decision they could change. Use connected feedback from later reviews to focus follow-up investigation. Preserve resolved answers; do not repeat questions without new evidence. Keep artifacts proportional to the task. Use generated evidence when available; otherwise identify the supplied source that covers a skipped stage. Never invent missing evidence or approval.

Own the observed current state. Put evidence next to each finding. Distinguish supplied claims, inspected code, and observed runtime behavior. Keep raw investigation output out of the main review and do not turn proposals into facts. Keep artifacts proportional to the task. Use generated evidence when available; otherwise identify the supplied source that covers a skipped stage. Never invent missing evidence or approval.

Map product outcomes to responsible system components. Group technical changes by responsibility, with current-to-proposed comparisons. Use data cards, interface cards, and state diagrams where useful. Highlight feasibility findings that change product behavior. Proposed code is useful only when it resolves an important ambiguity. Keep artifacts proportional to the task. Use generated evidence when available; otherwise identify the supplied source that covers a skipped stage. Never invent missing evidence or approval.

Assess only the connected final reviewed document against the supplied product design. Report whether it explicitly leaves a consequential unknown requiring investigation and whether feasibility findings require changing agreed product behavior. Include concise evidence in reason. Ordinary caveats or already recorded future work do not imply a new unknown. Do not rewrite artifacts or approve work. Supply evidence only; the daemon evaluates it. Keep the response brief.
